The **Columbia University Graduate School of Business** ,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-2) [branded as](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_name "Trade name") **Columbia Business School** (**CBS**),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-3) is the [business school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_school "Business school") of [Columbia University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University"), a [private](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_university "Private university") [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). Established in 1916, Columbia Business School is one of six [Ivy League business schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League_business_schools "Ivy League business schools") and one of the oldest business schools in the world.
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Columbia_Business_School&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/a/a0/Columbia_University_Bulletin_Graduate_School_of_Business_1978_1980.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Columbia_University_Bulletin_Graduate_School_of_Business_1978_1980.jpg)Bulletin for 1978–1980, when known as the Graduate School of Business
The school was founded in 1916 with 11 full-time faculty members and an inaugural class of 61 students, including 8 women. Banking executive Emerson McMillin provided initial funding in 1916, while [A. Barton Hepburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._Barton_Hepburn "A. Barton Hepburn"), then president of [Chase National Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_National_Bank "Chase National Bank"), provided funding for the school's endowment in 1919. The school expanded rapidly, enrolling 420 students by 1920, and in 1924 added a PhD program to the existing BS and MS degree programs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-5)
In 1945, Columbia Business School authorized the awarding of the MBA degree. Shortly thereafter, in the 1950s, the school adopted the [Hermes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermes "Hermes") emblem as its symbol, reflecting the entrepreneurial nature of the Greek god Hermes and his association with business, commerce, and communication.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-6) In 1952, the school admitted its last class of undergraduates.
The school currently offers executive education programs that culminate in a Certificate in Business Excellence (CIBE) and full alumni status, and several degree programs for the MBA and PhD degrees. In addition to the full-time MBA, the school offers four Executive MBA programs: the NY-EMBA Friday/Saturday program, the EMBA-Global program (launched in 2001 in conjunction with the [London Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Business_School "London Business School")), the EMBA-Americas program launched in 2012,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-7) and the EMBA-Global Asia program (launched in 2009 in conjunction with the London Business School and the [University of Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hong_Kong "University of Hong Kong") Business School). Students in jointly run programs earn an MBA degree from each of the cooperating institutions.
In 2004, economist [R. Glenn Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._Glenn_Hubbard "R. Glenn Hubbard") became Columbia Business School's eleventh dean. He was succeeded in 2019 by [Costis Maglaras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costis_Maglaras "Costis Maglaras").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-8)
## Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Columbia_Business_School&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Campus")]
From 1961, Columbia Business School was primarily located housed in Uris Hall, at the center of Columbia's [Morningside Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morningside_Heights "Morningside Heights") campus.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-9)
In October 2010, Columbia Business School announced that alumnus [Henry Kravis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Kravis "Henry Kravis"), the billionaire co-founder of private-equity firm [KKR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohlberg_Kravis_Roberts "Kohlberg Kravis Roberts"), pledged $100 million to fund an expansion of Columbia Business School, the largest gift in its history. The donation went toward construction of the business school's new site on Columbia's [Manhattanville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattanville "Manhattanville") campus.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-10) In December 2012, [Ronald Perelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Perelman "Ronald Perelman") also donated $100 million to the construction of the second business school building. In September 2021, [David Geffen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Geffen "David Geffen") pledged $75 million to support the new campus' construction.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-11) The buildings are designed by [Diller Scofidio + Renfro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diller_Scofidio_+_Renfro "Diller Scofidio + Renfro"), and are named Henry R. Kravis Hall and David Geffen Hall, respectively.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-12) Columbia Business School officially moved to Manhattanville in January 2022.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-13)
The cost of the new campus, which stands at $600 million, makes it the most expensive business school ever built.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-14)

## MBA program

The Columbia MBA Program is one of the most competitive in the world with an admission rate of 13.6% for the Class of 2021.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-Byrne-15) Students in the class that entered in 2009 come from 61 countries and speak more than 50 languages.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-Columbia_Business_School_employment_report-16)
The revised core curriculum, launched in the fall of 2008, represents about 40% of the degree requirement.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-17) It consists of 2 full courses and 12 half-term courses including Corporate Finance, Financial Accounting, Managerial Statistics, Managerial Economics, Leadership, Operations Management, and Marketing Strategy.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-18) While the first year of the program is usually devoted to completing the requirements of the core curriculum, the second year provides students with the opportunity to choose from the more than 130 elective courses available at the school and supplement them with more than 4,000 graduate-level classes from the university's other graduate and professional schools.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-http-19) Among the most popular electives at Columbia Business School are the Economics of Strategic Behavior, Financial Statement Analysis and Earnings Quality, Launching New Ventures, Modern Political Economy, and the Seminar in Value Investing.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-http-19)
Columbia Business School has a firm grade non-disclosure policy, which states that students may refrain from disclosing specific class grades, [GPAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_Point_Average "Grade Point Average"), or transcripts until they accept full-time, post graduation positions.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-20)
Students enter Columbia's MBA program in two tracks. The traditional fall term is approximately 550 students, while the January term "J-Term" is approximately 200 students. Students entering in the fall are divided into eight clusters of approximately 65 students that take all first year core classes together. J-Term students are broken into three clusters.
The January-entry is similar to the August-entry option. January-entry students attend orientation in the spring, while August-entry students are beginning their second terms, and finish their core courses over the summer, while August-entry students participate in summer internships. In the fall of the second year, the two tracks become one, and all MBA students choose from the same pool of electives, gain access to the same career management resources, lead the same clubs, and graduate as a single class.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-21)

## Executive MBA programs
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Columbia_Business_School&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Executive MBA programs")]
Columbia offers various executive MBA programs.
The Executive MBA (EMBA) Friday/Saturday Program is a 20-month graduate program designed for individuals that are looking to enhance their education without interrupting their careers. The EMBA program is taught on campus at Columbia University by full-time faculty. The first year of classes consists of the same core curriculum as the Full-Time MBA program. Executive education is the focus of the second year. This Friday/Saturday program is targeted at individuals with approximately 10 years of work experience.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-43)
The Executive MBA (EMBA) Saturday Program is a 24-month graduate degree program designed for individuals that are looking to enhance their education, but cannot take any time away from work. This program is the same as the Friday/Saturday program, with the exception that classes only meet on Saturdays over a longer period of time.
In addition to the New York-based EMBA Program, Columbia offers three partner programs to meet the differing needs and geographical distribution of prospective students.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-44) Because students in the partner EMBA programs must satisfy the separate requirements of each school, they earn an MBA degree from each participating university. Likewise, they become alumni of each university and business school and may avail themselves of all programs and privileges afforded to alumni.
  * The EMBA-Global Americas & Europe program is a 20-month program administered in partnership with the London Business School. The program enrolls approximately 70 students from around the world per year. Courses are taught by the full-time faculty of both schools. During the first year, the core curriculum classes alternate monthly between the campuses of Columbia University and the London Business School. The core curriculum is similar to that offered in the regular EMBA programs offered separately by each school, but with a more transnational-business emphasis. Second year classes may be selected from the portfolio of EMBA classes offered at either or both partner schools.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Business_School#cite_note-45)
  * The EMBA-Global Asia, run jointly with the London Business School and the [University of Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hong_Kong "University of Hong Kong"). This 20-month program follows a curriculum similar to the EMBA-Global program. Classes are held in Hong Kong, London, New York, and Shanghai.
